sources.title: Quantitative spectral stability for the Robin Laplacian
sources.authors: Veronica Felli; Prasun Roychowdhury; Giovanni Siclari
sources.history: Only v1 in official history checked 2026-09-16
sources.read_scope: Introduction; main results; Section 3 functional setting; Section 4 corrector and spectral expansion/proof; Section 5 statements; Section 6 coefficient comparison
sources.gap: Sharp general planar nodal-hole coefficient not proved; Theorem 2.4 loses an arbitrary power, Theorem 2.8 treats disks. Remark 2.10 leaves multiplicities for future research.
sources.existing_ingredients_used: Uniform H1 extension, small-hole trace bound, coercive shift, spectral convergence.
sources.normalization_concern: Derivative-based Theorem 2.8 needs comparison with explicit harmonic-polynomial coefficients; no public correction claim made.

sources.title: Quantitative spectral stability for the Neumann Laplacian in domains with small holes
sources.history: v1 2023-11-10; v2 2024-12-19; v3 2025-03-04. Latest comment clarifies connected complement.
sources.read_scope: Introduction and main theorems, relevant blow-up statements
sources.comparison: General sharp scaling-hole blow-up theorem assumes dimension at least three; planar explicit theorem treats round holes. Neumann analogue and perturbative method require attribution.

sources.title: On the splitting of Neumann eigenvalues in perforated domains
sources.history: Only v1, 2026-01-19, in inspected official history
sources.read_scope: Introduction and all main statements reread, including Theorems 1.1, 1.3 and 1.6; earlier pertinent reduction statements
sources.comparison: Generic-center multiplicity reduction for a spherical Neumann hole and complete splitting of double eigenvalues are prior work. General planar all-order Robin coefficients and fixed-center arbitrary-multiplicity complete splitting are the present claim.

sources.title: An Asymptotic Formula for Eigenvalues of the Neumann Laplacian in Domains with a Small Star-shaped Hole
sources.history: Only v1, 2024-06-04, in inspected official history
sources.read_scope: Boundary conditions, Theorem 2.1, Remark 2.2; proof only partly inspected
sources.comparison: Outer Dirichlet, hole Neumann, smooth star-shaped hole. Theorem 2.1 displays an area-only coefficient. Proposed ellipse coefficient differs; a complete spectral counterexample in matching hypotheses has not been established in this investigation.

sources.title: Singular variation of domain and spectra of the Laplacian with small Robin conditional boundary I
sources.access: Final PDF downloaded, 15 PDF pages including repository cover
sources.read_scope: Printed pages 837-838 visually inspected; wider extraction read selectively
sources.comparison: Smooth planar outer Dirichlet domain, circular hole, condition u+kappa*epsilon^sigma*normal_derivative(u)=0, kappa>0. Fixed positive Robin corresponds to sigma=0, with stated leading term and O(epsilon^(1+beta)) remainder, beta<1. Not a stated arbitrary-hole nodal two-term formula.

sources.title: Singular variation of domain and spectra of the Laplacian with small Robin conditional boundary II
sources.read_scope: Printed pages 403-405 visually inspected; first several proof sections text-screened
sources.comparison: Same circular-hole, outer-Dirichlet setting; Theorems 1-2 treat sigma>=1 and sigma<0. The fixed Robin sigma=0 case is referred to Part I.

sources.title: Simple Neumann eigenvalues for the Laplace operator in a domain with a small hole
sources.access: Publisher abstract/metadata only; institution repository lists restricted PDF
sources.comparison: Abstract establishes analytic dependence in epsilon and epsilon log epsilon in even dimensions. Full coefficient and scope comparison remains necessary; no claim of priority over it.

sources.title: Layer potential techniques in spectral analysis. Part I: Complete asymptotic expansions for eigenvalues of the Laplacian in domains with small inclusions
sources.access: AMS journal-path PDF 403, CiteSeer direct retrieval timeout; preserved in priority-retrieval-2.json; full text unread
sources.comparison: Author-uploaded abstract and introductory indexed text describe arbitrary-shape conductivity inclusions and complete expansions, with Neumann outer boundary. General expansion methods are credited. Full theorem comparison remains incomplete; no separate novelty claim for the logarithmic scalar coefficient.

sources.title: Asymptotic behavior of repeated eigenvalues of perturbed self-adjoint elliptic operators
sources.access: Publisher abstract/bibliography; ETH API route returned 429 and alternate bitstream download route returned 500; full theorem comparison pending
sources.comparison: Final article still unread. Related 2017 SAM report inspected separately; its leading matrix applications do not give the all-order fixed-center Robin construction. No assertion that report and final text are identical.

sources.title: Corrigendum to Ramification of multiple eigenvalues for the Dirichlet-Laplacian in perforated domains
sources.authors: Laura Abatangelo; Corentin Lena; Paolo Musolino
sources.history: Only v1 in official history checked 2026-09-16; displayed submission date 2026-05-07 differs from identifier month and is preserved as displayed.
sources.access: Full author HTML and official history downloaded with hashes
sources.read_scope: Sections 1-5, including finite-dimensional proofs and corrected two-order example
sources.comparison: The vanishing-order filtration, projection reduction and Schur-complement correction are prior work. Proposed Robin extension must establish its own weighted PDE estimates; no novelty claimed for the matrix mechanism.
sources.full_proof_audited: Read and compared by originating assistant; not independent review

sources.title: The generalized polarization tensors for resolved imaging. Part I: Shape reconstruction of a conductivity inclusion
sources.authors: Habib Ammari; Hyeonbae Kang; Mikyoung Lim; Habib Zribi
sources.access: Author-hosted abstract and indexed primary excerpts; direct PDF TLS handshake timeout
sources.read_scope: Abstract and indexed shape-derivative discussion only
sources.comparison: Shape derivatives of generalized polarization tensors and Fourier mode selectivity are prior work. Complete fixed-center Robin spectral splitting is the candidate application; full text not compared.

sources.title: Splitting a multiple eigenvalue in the boundary value problem for a membrane clamped on a small part of the boundary
sources.comparison: Prior complete splitting under a shrinking Dirichlet patch on a Neumann boundary; full text not compared.

sources.title: A variational principle for the perturbation of repeated eigenvalues and applications
sources.read_scope: Introduction, abstract variational principle and its proof, stability/genericity statements, all application statements and discussion in Sections 4.2-4.5; final bibliography inspected
sources.comparison: Grounded-hole application has one leading evaluation branch. Conductivity application has a gradient polarization matrix, leaving vanishing leading directions in the remainder. Boundary deformation is also considered. These applications do not construct a fixed-center homothetic Robin hole splitting every finite cluster. Final 2022 article is not assumed identical.

priority_questions: Does prior layer-potential or analytic-expansion theory already give the arbitrary Lipschitz planar Robin nodal coefficient and the explicit second term?
How much novelty is in the sharp nodal-order identification, as opposed to an application of an existing full expansion?
Is the nonnodal epsilon^2 log epsilon coefficient already explicit for fixed-sign Robin holes of general shape?
Resolve coefficient-normalization and anisotropy consistency concerns before using them as arguments for novelty.
Determine whether the proposed arbitrary-Lipschitz planar Robin all-branch law, after attribution of the 2026 corrected Dirichlet matrix mechanism, is a distinct substantial contribution.
Is the fixed-center, one-shape, all-finite-window complete Robin splitting consequence already proved in singular-perturbation or polarization-tensor literature?
significance_assessment: Provisionally favorable for the combined all-order planar PDE law and one-shape fixed-center complete splitting; see ASSESSMENT.md. Target-journal suitability and priority remain revisable.
